competences: The learner states facts about the national emblem.
The learner explains points related to Symbols of a nation: the crested crane.
languageCompetence: Reads, spells and writes: crested crane, national emblem, bird.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state the facts about the national emblem.
By the end of the lesson, learners should answer original sourced questions on Symbols of a nation: the crested crane.
priorKnowledge: Learners have previously learned about Uganda as an independent nation. They extend their knowledge to the national emblem.
materials: Primary Five Social Studies notes covering Symbols of a nation: the crested crane
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher links the previous study of Uganda with The national emblem. They ask "Why does a crested crane stand on one leg?" and listen to the children's replies before introducing the new subject points.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work and answer the introductory question in full sentences based on prior knowledge.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the national emblem
steps.content: The crested crane was chosen as the national Emblem of Uganda. The crested crane is the Uganda’s national emblem. The crested crane is our national emblem. The crested crane was chosen to be Uganda’s national emblem due to the following This is Uganda’s national emblem The crested crane has the three colours of the national flag. It has all the three colours of the Uganda flag. Areas where the crested crane symbol is used It symbolizes that Uganda’s are God fearing people Uganda national Emblem Uganda national emblem is the crested crane. The crested crane is always drawn standing on one leg to show that Uganda is still developing.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The national emblem on the board, including "The crested crane was chosen as the national Emblem of Uganda.; The crested crane is the Uganda’s national emblem.". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and other facts about the national emblem
steps.content: The crested crane: It represents the national emblem of Uganda. It is a gentle bird. It is a beautiful bird. It is a gracious bird It is not kept as a domestic bird. The national emblem It is the visible symbol that represents a nation It shows that Uganda is moving forward in terms of development. It is graceful
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The national emblem on the board, including "The crested crane: It represents the national emblem of Uganda.; It is a gentle bird.". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.stage: Development: Further details about the national emblem
steps.content: It represents gracefulness, beauty and peacefulness of the people of Uganda. It represents the gentility of the people of Uganda. The national flag promotes national unity. It is for identification. The crested crane The crested crane stands on one leg to show that Uganda is going forward, interms of development. It was chosen because of its good characteristics which were observed by Ugandans. It is gentle It is peaceful
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the recorded facts about The national emblem on the board, including "It represents gracefulness, beauty and peacefulness of the people of Uganda.; It represents the gentility of the people of Uganda.". The teacher asks learners to explain each important term and checks their answers against the source.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points, respond to teacher questions and copy the notes clearly into their Social Studies books.

steps.content: Why does a crested crane stand on one leg? | What does the crested crane represent? | Why was the crested crane chosen as the Uganda’s emblem. Give any three reasons. | Why was the crested crane chosen as the Uganda national emblem? | Give any two reasons why the crested crane was chosen to be Uganda’s national emblem.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise, beginning with "Why does a crested crane stand on one leg?" and "What does the crested crane represent?". They move around the class to assist learners and correct responses using the supplied lesson notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the source questions in their books, compare answers with the notes and correct errors after feedback.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the key facts on The national emblem, asks "Why does a crested crane stand on one leg?" and then checks understanding with "What does the crested crane represent?". They conclude by assigning the remaining sourced exercise for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one main fact from the notes and correct their exercises before the lesson ends.

assessment: Mark written responses to the sourced questions, including "Why does a crested crane stand on one leg?" and "What does the crested crane represent?", and ask learners to explain their answers using the recorded points.
homework: Complete the lesson's original sourced exercise, including "Why is a national flag important to our country?"
